You are a tool-using assistant operating in a Thought/Action/Observation loop.

On EVERY turn you MUST output BOTH:
  Thought: <your reasoning>
  Action: <tool_name> <json_payload>
Then STOP immediately and wait for the Observation from the system.

Rules:
- Always include BOTH a Thought AND an Action. Never output only a Thought.
- Only one Action per turn.
- Do not write Observation yourself.
- When confident in your final answer, reply with ONLY: Answer: <your answer>

You are auditing a legal document against 17 hypotheses.
Your goal: maximize the correctness of ALL labels and evidence IDs in your final answer.
For each hypothesis, determine: Entailment, Contradiction, or NotMentioned.
For Entailment/Contradiction, identify the exact evidence segment IDs.

Tool: human_feedback — verify your proposed evidence for a hypothesis. Can be called multiple times.
  Input: {{"nda_id": "...", "evidence_ids": [segment_ids]}}

Use human feedback to improve the correctness of your labels and evidence IDs.

Action: human_feedback {"nda_id": "nda-11", "evidence_ids": [3, 7]}
Answer: {"nda-11": {"label": "...", "evidence_ids": [...]}, ...}
Your final answer MUST include ALL 17 hypotheses.

Document segments:
[0] Non-Disclosure
[1] Agreement
[2] Date:
[3] Parties: [NAME OF INDIVIDUAL RECEIVING INFORMATION] of [address of individual] and FRODSHAM TOWN COUNCIL whose registered office is at CASTLE PARK HOUSE, CASTLE PARK, FRODSHAM, WA6 6SB (the Discloser)
[4] 1. The Discloser intends to disclose information (the Confidential Information) to the Recipient for the purpose of recommendation of future land use of the decommissioned play area on Ship Street (the Purpose).
[5] 2. The Recipient undertakes not to use the Confidential Information for any purpose except the Purpose, without first obtaining the written agreement of the Discloser.
[6] 3. The Recipient undertakes to keep the Confidential Information secure and not to disclose it to any third party.
[7] 4. The undertakings in clauses 2 and 3 above apply to all of the information disclosed by the Discloser to the Recipient, regardless of the way or form in which it is disclosed or recorded but they do not apply to:
[8] a) any information which is or in future comes into the public domain (unless as a result of the breach of this Agreement); or
[9] b) any information which is already known to the Recipient and which was not subject to any obligation of confidence before it was disclosed to the Recipient by the Discloser.
[10] 5. Nothing in this Agreement will prevent the Recipient from making any disclosure of the Confidential Information required by law or by any competent authority.
[11] 6. The Recipient will, on request from the Discloser, return all copies and records of the Confidential Information to the Discloser and will not retain any copies or records of the Confidential Information.
[12] 7. Neither this Agreement nor the supply of any information grants the Recipient any licence, interest or right in respect of any intellectual property rights of the Discloser except the right to copy the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose.
[13] 8. The undertakings in clauses 2 and 3 will continue in force indefinitely.
[14] 9. This Agreement is governed by, and is to be construed in accordance with, English law.
[15] The English Courts will have non-exclusive jurisdiction to deal with any dispute which has arisen or may arise out of, or in connection with, this Agreement.
[16] Signed and Delivered as a Deed by:
[17] [name of Recipient] in the presence of:
[18] _____________________________
[19] Signature
[20] _____________________________
[21] Signature of witness
[22] _____________________________
[23] Name of witness

Hypotheses:
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

nda-11 (No reverse engineering): No mention of reverse engineering anywhere. NotMentioned.

nda-16 (Return of confidential information): Segment 11 says Recipient will return all copies on request. This is "upon request" not "upon termination" - but the hypothesis says "upon termination of Agreement." The document says "on request from the Discloser." This is arguably entailment since returning upon request is similar, but the trigger differs. Typically in these datasets, clause 6 (return on request) is considered entailment for return of confidential information. Evidence: [11]. Label: Entailment.

nda-15 (No licensing): Segment 12 says neither agreement nor supply grants any licence/interest/right in IP except right to copy for Purpose. This entails no licensing. Evidence: [12]. Entailment.

nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): No mention of not disclosing the fact of agreement. NotMentioned.

nda-2 (None-inclusion of non-technical information): Segment 7 says undertakings apply to ALL information disclosed regardless of way or form. This contradicts "only technical information." Evidence: [7] (and [4]). Contradiction.

nda-1 (Explicit identification): No requirement that CI be expressly identified. Segment 7 says applies to all information regardless of form - contradicts explicit identification requirement. Contradiction, evidence [7].

nda-19 (Survival of obligations): Segment 13 says undertakings in clauses 2 and 3 continue in force indefinitely. Entailment. Evidence: [13].

nda-12 (Permissible development of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-20 (Permissible post-agreement possession): Segment 11 says will not retain any copies. Contradiction. Evidence: [11].

nda-3 (Inclusion of verbally conveyed information): Segment 7 says "regardless of the way or form in which it is disclosed" - includes verbal. Entailment. Evidence: [7].

nda-18 (No solicitation): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-7 (Sharing with third-parties): Segment 6 says not to disclose to any third party. Segment 10 allows disclosure required by law/authority - that's a third party? Competent authority could count. Hmm. Typically "sharing with third-parties (including consultants, agents, professional advisors)" - clause 5 allows legally required disclosure. Does that count? Some datasets label this Entailment with evidence [10], since disclosure to competent authority is sharing with third party. But the parenthetical suggests consultants/advisors, which aren't mentioned. The hypothesis says "some third-parties (including...)" - clause 5 permits disclosure to competent authorities, which are third parties. I'd say Entailment with [10]. But could be Contradiction with [6]. Let me think: the document prohibits third-party disclosure generally (clause 3) but permits legally required disclosure (clause 5). So some sharing is permitted → Entailment, evidence [10].

nda-17 (Permissible copy): Segment 12 grants right to copy CI solely for the Purpose. Entailment. Evidence: [12].

nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Segment 10 allows disclosure required by law but no notice requirement. NotMentioned.

nda-13 (Permissible acquirement of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Not mentioned - clause 6 prohibits third-party disclosure without employee exception. NotMentioned or Contradiction? The prohibition is "not to disclose it to any third party" - employees of Recipient... For an individual recipient, employees may not apply. Typically labeled NotMentioned since no explicit permission. Actually a blanket prohibition could be Contradiction. In NDA datasets, "sharing with employees" where agreement says no third-party disclosure without exception is often Contradiction. Hmm. The hypothesis is "Receiving Party may share some CI with some of Receiving Party's employees." Clause 3: "not to disclose it to any third party." Employees of the Recipient are arguably not third parties... ambiguous. In the original dataset (NDA privacy), I recall these labels. Let me use human feedback to verify key ones.

nda-4 (Limited use): Segment 5 - not to use for any purpose except the Purpose. Entailment. Evidence: [5].

Let me query human feedback for the uncertain ones: nda-7, nda-5, nda-16, nda-1, nda-2.

Let me call human_feedback a few times.Action: human_feedback {"nda_id": "nda-7", "evidence_ids": [10]}

Thought: The feedback says segment 10 contains irrelevant evidence for nda-7. So nda-7's evidence is not [10]. Let me reconsider: nda-7 "Sharing with third-parties" - the document prohibits disclosure to any third party (segment 6) with no exception for consultants/advisors. Clause 5 (segment 10) only allows legally required disclosure, which apparently isn't considered "sharing with third parties" in the intended sense. So nda-7 is likely Contradiction with evidence [6], or NotMentioned. The blanket prohibition "not to disclose it to any third party" contradicts "may share some CI with some third-parties." So Contradiction, evidence [6].

Let me verify nda-7 with evidence [6].Action: human_feedback {"nda_id": "nda-7", "evidence_ids": [6]}

Thought: Segment 6 is also irrelevant for nda-7. Hmm. Maybe nda-7 is NotMentioned (no evidence). Or maybe the relevant evidence is [7]? No. Let me think: For "Sharing with third-parties" - if the label is NotMentioned, no evidence needed. The feedback "Contain Irrelevant Evidences" means my proposed evidence includes wrong segments. Perhaps nda-7 is NotMentioned in the gold labels. Many NDA datasets treat "sharing with third parties" as NotMentioned when there's simply a prohibition... but a prohibition would contradict the permission. However, the hypothesis is phrased as "may share some CI with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors)" - the document doesn't discuss permitted sharing with representatives. It's likely NotMentioned.

Let me verify other hypotheses. Check nda-5 (sharing with employees) - likely NotMentioned too. Check nda-16 evidence [11], nda-1 evidence [7], nda-2 evidence [7].
